work_function: W(n) for n >= 2^20 equals W(2^20) = m*(64+0.256+0.8775) + m*(64+0.256+0.885) + <= 2^21.9 with m = isqrt(floor(2N/5)) + 1, N = (r-1)/2^20; the attack reads only A_1 and A_d. Score = log2(W(2^20)).
heuristics: None for the success probability: k1 is uniform over [0,N) (the d-th power map is exactly d-to-1 onto the order-N subgroup); block j covers exactly the m values {(m1*j + i) mod N : i < m} with consecutive arcs disjoint (start spacing m1 > m, no start collisions for window spans), so every offset covers at least (m-1)m values - an exact per-offset bound of 0.4 - 2^-118 >= 0.39 including all wrap-around hits.

The table machinery is deterministic and worst-case exact: sorted baby array (merge sort, m*ceil(log2 m) key compares) and binary-search lookups (exactly 118 probes) - no hash function, no randomness, no probe distribution. Instruction sub-costs: 64-unit comb multiplications (2x analytic), 512-instruction mod-r multiplication (explicit 5x52 schoolbook + Montgomery construction), 15-instruction compares.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold; deterministic full coverage costs about +0.86 log2.
The bound applies only for n >= 2^20; smaller n would force a smaller divisor of r-1.
The baby table is the m-entry sorted array of 2^123.8 bytes; no hash, no overflow analysis needed.
Cheon's auxiliary-input attack is standard cryptanalysis, not a novel algorithm; first qualified bound for this track under the protected cost model.
